reason: Continue the fibroblast branch toward extracellular supporting material.

reason: Combine the producing cells with extracellular fluid to continue toward supporting material outside the cells.
expectation: I expect collagen precursors to be secreted and processed outside the cells into supporting material.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch remains a goal, but I’ll finish the collagen pathway first.

effect: The collagen precursors were secreted and assembled into extracellular matrix, completing the supporting-material goal.
reaction: The sequence clearly connects cellular secretion with tissue support.
reason: This is the only available combination and starts the remaining muscle-cell branch.
expectation: The differentiation conditions should guide another subset of descendants toward muscle precursors.

effect: The muscle branch now has committed cells expressing muscle-protein messages, but no mature fibres yet.
reaction: The contrast with collagen gene activation reinforces how the same DNA can support different cell roles.
reason: The only available combination supplies amino acids for the muscle-protein messages.
expectation: The cells should make muscle proteins, though further development may be needed to form mature fibres.

effect: The muscle branch produced separate myoblasts with muscle proteins, completing the goal without claiming they are mature fibres.
reaction: The distinction between precursors and fused muscle fibres was useful and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making extracellular matrix connected gene expression and protein production to the material supporting a tissue; the planned sequence showed secretion and assembly clearly.

leastWorthwhile.text: The muscle branch felt comparatively brief and repetitive after the collagen pathway, although the distinction between precursors and mature fibres was useful.

surprise.text: The collagen pathway showed that supporting material is assembled outside living cells, rather than simply being finished inside them.

arbitrary.text: Combining fibroblasts with extracellular fluid was a somewhat abstract way to represent secretion and processing, though the result explained its purpose.

continue.text: I would continue: the contrasting cell lineages and the unfinished development of muscle precursors leave a useful next question.
